messages:
alex: FYI Trivy run on prod images popped a few high/critical CVEs in our base images (OpenSSL + glibc variants). Thought we should triage and decide rebuild/prioritization today. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-3421 :eyes:

maya: Can you paste the scan output? which images/tags affected? alpine vs ubuntu? CVSS scores?

alex: Paste below. Mostly two clusters: alpine:3.17 images show openssl CVE-2025-0001 (CVSS 9.1) and ubuntu:22.04-jammy images show glibc CVE-2024-5678 (CVSS 7.8). Trivy output (trimmed):

```
alpine:3.17/worker:latest
  - openssl CVE-2025-0001 HIGH  (linked libssl)
  - libcrypto CVE-2025-0002 MEDIUM

ubuntu:22.04/runtime:202402
  - glibc CVE-2024-5678 HIGH (nscd/ld.so)
  - openssl CVE-2025-0001 HIGH
```

alex: Affected services are: image-builder, inference-worker (dedicated pool), and some helper sidecars.

samir: Thanks. My initial read: openssl CVE has an available patch in upstream alpine edge and ubuntu security repos. glibc fix for jammy is in -security but may require rebuild/retag to pick up libc update.

jordan: tagging infra for release pipeline implications. @jordan can our immutable image pipeline rebuild images and run smoke tests automatically?

jordan: yes, buildkite pipeline can kick a full-rebuild for specific base tags. I can add a job that rebuilds all images that use base:alpine:3.17 and base:ubuntu:22.04-jammy, run unit+smoke, then push to canary repo (canary/). Need approvals for prod promotion.

maya: Prioritization suggestion: 1) openssl CVE on alpine (CVSS 9.1) — immediate rebuild and patch, 2) glibc jammy (7.8) — medium-high, schedule ASAP but test longer, 3) lower-medium deps follow. Thoughts?

samir: +1. Also check musl vs glibc linkage for our binaries. Some static-linked tools might not be affected. We should generate SBOMs per image to confirm which packages are actually in use.

alex: Agreed. Action items I propose:
- generate per-image SBOMs (syft) and attach to RED-3421
- run targeted rebuilds for alpine images with patched openssl and push to canary/
- run extended integration tests for any image picking up glibc updates before promoting
- update base-image tags in Dockerfiles to pinned patched tags and create PRs
- schedule a maintenance window if any service needs restart in prod

maya: Sounds good. Can we do a quick impact matrix in this thread? I can start:
- image-builder: uses ubuntu:22.04 -> moderate risk if libc updated; low restart pain
- inference-worker (dedicated): uses alpine:3.17 -> high risk for remote exploit, needs immediate rebuild + canary
- sidecar-logger: uses ubuntu -> low risk

jordan: Build actions: I'll add a buildkite pipeline job: `rebuild-base-patch` that accepts base tag list env var. Example: `BASE_TAGS=alpine:3.17,ubuntu:22.04-jammy` and it will run:

```bash
# pseudo
./scripts/rebuild_images.sh --bases "$BASE_TAGS" --sbom --smoke-tests
# artifacts: sbom.json, trivy-report.json, image-manifest.json
```

jordan: Will also add automatic creation of PRs that update Dockerfile FROM lines to pinned patched digest.

samir: On canary promotion: plan to promote to 10% traffic for inference-worker for 24h while monitoring latency and errors, and check for any cryptic ld.so errors post-glibc update. If issues, rollback by switching image tag back to previous digest.

alex: Who will own making the PRs and coordinating canary? Maya volunteer?

maya: I can take the alpine openssl rebuild and PRs. Samir can own the jammy glibc image testing. Jordan will wire the pipeline. Alex will own the triage ticket and communications.

infra-bot: buildkite job queued: rebuild-base-patch (alpine:3.17) — job id 78654

alex: ETA? Maya, can you push a canary by EOD? If not, we escalate to emergency patching tomorrow morning.

maya: I'll aim for EOD, likely 3-4 hours. Posting progress in RED-3421.

samir: I'll start the extended integration matrix on jammy images and post test plan here. Quick note: we may need to bump libc-dependent pinned versions for some prebuilt wheels.

jordan: CI will collect trivy scan and SBOM artifacts and attach to the ticket automatically. Also adding a retention tag for rollback window (48h).

alex: Thanks team. After canary success we get approvals and do a staged rollout across regions (us-east-1 then eu-west-1). If anything looks off, revert and open incident.

maya: quick command I used to repro locally: `trivy image --scanners vuln --format json alpine:3.17 | jq '.Results[].Vulnerabilities | length'`

alex: Good. I updated RED-3421 with the action owners and timeline. I'll ping on-call before prod promotions. :thumbsup:

jordan: noted. I'll leave the build job running and post logs when ready.

alex: closing loop — we'll reconvene here after canary results. Thanks!
